html:
The Wambaya are an Aboriginal people of the southern Barkly Tableland in the Northern Territory, a wide grassland east of Tennant Creek.

Their neighbours were the Jingili and Mudburra to the west, the Warumungu to the southwest and the Wakaya to the east. Their language is not part of the Pama-Nyungan family, and linguists know it for its unusually free word order.

From the 1880s large cattle stations took over the Barkly Tableland, and much of Wambaya land is still under them. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Wambaya are an Aboriginal people of the southern Barkly Tableland in the Northern Territory, a wide grassland east of Tennant Creek.
